code: fuzz_target receives raw HTTP request bytes from input file
note: Attacker-controlled input bytes enter the fuzzer entry point and are passed to the HTTP/1 parser.

code: HTTP request line and headers are parsed from input bytes
note: The parser extracts request metadata including Content-Length and transfer encoding from the raw input.

code: Request body entity is constructed from parsed Content-Length
note: A crafted Content-Length header causes the entity length to be set to a huge value, influencing subsequent buffer accounting.

code: size_t inbufcnt = ...; // derived from request entity buffer count
note: The number of input buffers is computed from the parsed request entity; a huge entity length leads to an inbufcnt value near SIZE_MAX.
VLA bound expression inbufcnt + 3 wraps around to a non-positive value when inbufcnt is SIZE_MAX-2 or SIZE_MAX-1, triggering UBSAN Non-positive-vla-bound-value.
The invalid VLA size is passed to the compiler/runtime, causing the UBSAN crash before any memory access.

code: h2o_socket_sendvec called with the invalid VLA buffer array
note: The crash stack shows h2o_socket_sendvec as the sink where the non-positive VLA bound is reported.
